clue.text: Aussie soldier late leaving bars possibly?

indicators.note: leaving means the word late departs from the longer word, so it is taken off

parts.note: chocolate is often sold in bars; 'possibly' says bars are only one example

explanation.surface: An Australian soldier is slow to leave the pubs, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like drinking places, but they are chocolate bars; 'leaving' takes LATE off. A choco (chocolate soldier) was Australian slang for a militiaman in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Choco was Australian slang for a militia conscript, thought to be a soldier who would melt in action.

clue.text: Pancreatic enzyme requiring time in pricy nosh I'm breaking down

indicators.note: in means the time letter goes inside the rearranged letters
breaking down means the letters of the pricy nosh fodder are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder as the setter meant it: the anagram needs MY where the clue prints I'm

explanation.surface: An expensive meal being digested needs time, with the enzyme doing the breaking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' should turn the fodder into CHYMORYPSIN for 'in' to take T; but the enzyme has two Ys and one I, so the printed 'I'm' is the setter's slip for 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chymotrypsin is a digestive protease secreted by the pancreas into the small intestine.

clue.text: Confusion about cow tucking into rotten hay — it's lacking vital element

indicators.note: tucking into means the confusion-and-cow unit goes inside the rotten hay
rotten means the letters of hay are spoiled into a new order
about means the confusion word goes round the cow

parts.note: pi (or pie) is printers' jumbled type, so confusion
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A muddled cow buries itself in mouldy hay, which has lost its goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusion' is printers' pie, type in a jumble; 'about' wraps it round the cow to make POXI. 'rotten' shuffles the hay to HYA, and 'tucking into' sets POXI inside. The vital element is oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypoxia is a deficiency of oxygen reaching the body's tissues, the element life depends on.

clue.text: Author to put in work that's convertible

indicators.note: put in means the author-and-to letters are placed inside the work

parts.note: OP (opus) is a musical work
a pen is a writer, as in a hired pen

explanation.surface: A writer is asked to contribute to something that can be adapted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places PEN plus TO inside OP, the abbreviation for opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-top car has a roof that folds away, which is what a convertible is.

clue.text: What may be origin of a rug stood on by serious objector?

definitions.text: What may be origin of a rug stood on by serious objector?

indicators.note: stood on by means the objector sits above the rearranged letters in this down entry

parts.note: CO is a conscientious objector, someone serious about their beliefs

indicators.note: the letters of a rug may have come from a different word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pacifist stands on a rug made from an animal skin, and we wonder where it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What may be origin of' reworks the letters into UGAR, as if they came from something else; 'stood on by' puts the objector on top in this down entry. A big cat's skin might well end up as a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a big cat whose pelt could be made into a floor covering.

clue.text: Body bag sent back in carriages

indicators.note: in means the reversed bag goes inside the carriages

parts.note: cars are carriages, as on a train

indicators.note: sent back means the word for bag is turned round

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like part of an animal or plant

explanation.surface: A body bag is returned inside railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body bag' reads as one thing, but 'Body' alone is the definition; 'sent back' makes CAS, and 'in' puts it inside the carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is a dead body, especially of an animal.

clue.text: Mum's in grip of depression to do with optical defect?

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass in a mountain ridge
Mum is MA, and the 's stands for is

explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' sounds like low mood but is a col, a dip in a ridge; 'in grip of' holds MA inside it. Coma is the comet-shaped blur a lens gives off-axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Coma is a lens aberration making points look comet-like, and comal is its adjective.

clue.text: Contribution from American attorney can change the complexion of things!

explanation.definitionFit: Anatto (annatto) is an orange-red vegetable dye used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: Small radius in rubbish — it's not good for potato crop (7, two words)

definitions.text: it's not good for potato crop

parts.note: r is the symbol for radius, written small
grot is British slang for rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: Something small among the waste is bad news for a potato harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring rot is a bacterial disease of potatoes that rots a ring of the tuber's vascular tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring rot is a bacterial disease that spoils potato tubers, so it is bad for the crop.

clue.text: Dialect that is apparent in a parade (5, two words)

parts.note: a parade is a show or display

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dialect' labels the answer as a regional word: a-show means on show, visible.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect a-show means on show, so visible or evident.

clue.text: Maelstrom to be seen shortly in south-west Ireland

IRL is the abbreviation for Ireland, signalled by shortly

explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' means both places are given as abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl is a whirling eddy, a small version of a whirlpool.

clue.text: Casual 'Sorry' ensues about power that transcends feelings

casual means the letters of sorry and ensues are thrown together in a loose new order

clue.text: Bit of Haydn on toy piano upset sleeplike state

indicators.note: upset means the letters of toy piano are knocked over into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Hypotonia is abnormally low muscle tone, the limp slackness of a body at rest.

clue.text: Potter's creation to lift fellow's former morbid angst

hip (or hyp) is an old word for hypochondria or morbid low spirits

clue.text: Acceleration in ringtone? It may figure in Ulan Bator exchange

definitions.text: It may figure in Ulan Bator exchange

clue.text: One has to be put up with (unfortunately)!

definitions.text: One has to be put up with (unfortunately)!

parts.words: One has to be put up with (unfortunately)
parts.note: a tedious person is someone you have to tolerate, sadly; the word is also the past tense of bear, put up with

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a tiresome person you must endure, and the answer also happens to be the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious person whose company must be tolerated is the classic example of someone others endure.

clue.text: Chopped lox, including sea bream — it's nice in soup

chopped means the letters of lox are cut up and rearranged

parts.note: the tai is a Japanese sea bream

explanation.walkthrough: Lox is smoked salmon, which suits the soup picture, but 'Chopped' scrambles it to OXL, and 'including' puts the Japanese fish inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxtail is a classic soup ingredient, braised for a rich beefy stock.

clue.text: Tres only 50% needs something boring to work with in net

parts.note: only half of the letters of tres are kept, its first half

explanation.surface: Something about Spanish numbers and DIY tools, with a fishing net at the end.

clue.text: Point maybe raised uncertainty with senior administrator?

an elder is a senior church official

explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IF upwards to FI in this down entry. 'Point' looks like an argument, but it is a cricket fielding position, square on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Point is a cricket fielding position, so a player stationed there is a fielder.

clue.text: Dull place, almost antiquated, enveloped by disapproving noises

parts.note: boos are noises of disapproval from a crowd
nie is an archaic spelling of nigh, which means almost

explanation.walkthrough: 'antiquated' looks like a description of the dull place, but it marks an old spelling of nigh, which means almost; 'enveloped by' wraps the jeers round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The boonies is American slang, short for boondocks, for remote rural backwaters where nothing happens.

clue.text: Hindu deity, when not male, attracted centrally

parts.note: Indra is the Vedic king of the gods

indicators.note: not means the male letters are removed from when

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn means drawn inwards, pulled towards the centre.

clue.text: Old Uncle Reg, squiffy with second, comes into view?

parts.note: eme is an old word for uncle

indicators.note: squiffy means tipsy, so the letters of Reg stagger out of order

explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear from hiding or come out into the open.

clue.text: Pennsylvania sectarian obsessed about withdrawal of drink

indicators.note: about means the obsessed word goes round the reversed drink

parts.note: rapt means wholly absorbed or obsessed

indicators.note: withdrawal means the drink is drawn backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A Pennsylvania sect member is obsessed with giving up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rappists followed George Rapp, who settled in Pennsylvania. 'withdrawal of' makes PIS, and 'about' wraps the obsessed word round it; the talk of giving up drink suits a puritan sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Rappists were members of George Rapp's Harmony Society, a celibate religious community founded in Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Horse among stallions in hunting areas?

indicators.note: among means the horse letter goes in among the stallions

parts.note: sires are stallions used for breeding
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: One horse mixes with the studs out in fox-hunting country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' fits the picture but is heroin, H, and 'among' places it inside SIRES. The Shires are the English Midland counties famed for fox-hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shires are the English Midland counties, long renowned as the heart of fox-hunting country.

clue.text: Gushing dunny, loo without opening

indicators.note: without opening means the first letter of loo is dropped

explanation.definitionFit: Too-too means excessively effusive or extravagant, which is what gushing praise is.

clue.text: Rod with last of catch on the end, about 3 metres in length

parts.note: a cane is a rod or stick

parts.note: the final letter of catch is kept

clue.text: Reproduction round piano stool

indicators.note: round means the reproduction goes around the piano letter

parts.note: a copy is a reproduction

explanation.definitionFit: A coppy, or coppy stool, is a dialect word for a small low stool.

clue.text: Indefinite article, unknown one on something hypothesized by physicists

x is the usual algebraic unknown
I is the Roman numeral one

clue.text: Court room, private — not very exciting

a den is a private room

explanation.surface: A judge's private room in court is a dull place.

explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is stiff and lifeless, so dull.

clue.text: In which for countrymen I'll replace centre of shell

the I of I'll is the letter that does the replacing

clue.text: Scots leather we hear (though not exactly Scots style) is OK for these crags

clue.text: Spray special lemur on foot

parts.note: the indri is a large Madagascan lemur

clue.text: English let off with force surrounding border house, fortified

clue.text: Scandinavian tongue — with it I'll perplex Yorks inn

clue.text: Buxom as a Scots lassie, year after children?
